 Ayotte among governors calling on Congress to boost home heating aid as need grows
 New Hampshire Public Radio | 
 By
 NHPR Staff 
 Published November 12, 2026 at 3:45 PM EST
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Dan Tuohy 
 / 
 NHPR Gov. Kelly Ayotte and governors from other New England states are calling on Congress to fund an additional $3 Billion for the federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program amid an uptick in requests for heating help as winter looms. 
 Noting a “sense of urgency,” Gov. Kelly Ayotte has joined other New England governors in calling on Congress to fund an additional $3 billion in home heating assistance.
 The money for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, a federal program commonly called LIHEAP , would be an allocation for the country, not just New England.
 The proposed appropriation would about double the funding New Hampshire receives to assist families with heating costs. It comes as heating oil prices are up 72% compared to last year.
 Ayotte noted New Hampshire and other New England states have been hit hard for high home heating costs.
 “With costs being higher, it’s important to have more of those resources,” she said Tuesday. “And you heard there’s a thousand applicant increase, so those resources are important and they’re going to be needed.”
 The home heating assistance has bipartisan support, according to the governor.
 Ayotte said Tuesday that she also supports a regional pipeline project to bring more natural gas to the region. “And then, I think we also need to continue to hold the utilities accountable for money that they owe to ratepayers,” she said, “and that’s something that I’ve also worked with other New England governors on.”
 Families can apply for heating assistance at their local community action partnership office.
 The Fuel Assistance Program , which is the state’s arm for LIHEAP, provides benefits that range from $188 to $2,500, depending on household income and energy costs.
